claims.text: The additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has an fcc matrix.
Under elevated-temperature oxidizing conditions, degradation is governed by selective oxidation of Al and Ti.
Al and Ti are the most reactive elements in this alloy under the proposed exposure conditions.
Selective oxidation produces a continuous brittle oxide scale.
The oxide scale forms both at grain boundaries and on the alloy surface.
The oxide scale consists predominantly of Al2O3 and/or TiOx.
Selective oxidation of Al and Ti causes rapid formation of the brittle oxide layer.
Thermal-expansion mismatch between the oxide scale and the fcc matrix induces high localized stresses at elevated temperature.
The mismatch-induced stresses cause oxide-scale spallation and crack formation.
Scale spallation and cracking produce stress concentrators and localized embrittlement.
The resulting stress concentration and embrittlement promote catastrophic failure.
Reducing oxygen partial pressure will decrease the rate of oxide-scale formation relative to the baseline oxidizing atmosphere.
Reducing oxygen partial pressure will decrease the continuity of the oxide scale relative to baseline.
Reduced scale formation will delay oxide-induced crack initiation.
Samples exposed at reduced oxygen partial pressure will have lower crack density than baseline samples.
Samples exposed at reduced oxygen partial pressure will retain better mechanical integrity and exhibit longer time to catastrophic failure than baseline samples.
Selective oxidation is a known degradation mechanism in similar alloys.
